items.title: /teach entry choice: two doors, one pipeline — the file card leads and the five-step strip is the same for both
/teach/upload first look: three ways in are all present at once, and the privacy sentence is above the fold before any file is chosen
jsonl through the file picker: chip → node report → preview, and a teaching key is created silently with a backup link
Drag-and-drop onto the zone, and the same zone opened from the keyboard
Paste a table instead: two spreadsheet columns become a .tsv the NODE parses
Format help and the three sample datasets: download one, or start from it in one click
CSV with a header and values containing commas inside quotes
Header detection both ways: Korean column names are recognised, a headerless TSV keeps its first line as data
Plain text: the Q:/A: layout the format help promises
Alpaca and ChatML: the two shapes people already have on disk are read without an export step
Encodings: UTF-8 BOM + CRLF is silent, EUC-KR/cp949 and UTF-16 are read and SAID so
'Wrong columns or separator?' re-reads the bytes the node already has — no re-upload, new revision, new fingerprint
Size cap: a 5.1 MB file is refused in the browser before a byte is uploaded, and the node refuses it independently
Row caps: the 'Choose which 200' lesson banner, and the over-2000 dataset note that says nothing was hidden
Nothing usable in the file: 0 bytes, binary rubbish, a wrong file type, and a header with no data rows
A file that is all duplicates: one question kept, every later copy shown with the line it repeats
A messy real-world file: contradictions, over-length, a missing answer, an unreadable line — all counted, none hidden
Privacy notice and retention: 'Delete my file as soon as training finishes' is offered before the upload and honoured in the record
A visitor with no teaching key: nothing is owned, nothing is 401-ing in their face, and the key is created at the exact moment it is needed
한국어 toggle: the file door, the format examples and the error copy all switch, and the pipeline does not
The whole file door on a 360 px phone: nothing scrolls sideways and the question table becomes cards
Preview table: ok vs tidied-up rows, the tidy-up receipt and the same verdicts in Korean
Two answers for one question block both copies, and 'Keep this answer' resolves the contradiction
Too long: the pill names the real length and the node's limit, and the edit sheet refuses the same text
A half-filled line says which half is missing
A topic the operator blocks is refused per row, and the regex itself is validated
Lines the node could not read never enter the table — they are listed and counted underneath
The Line column is the line of the uploaded file: header, blank lines and a quoted newline all counted the node's way
After the first edit the report is rebuilt: rejected lines disappear and the numbers stop being file lines
Changing a question throws away every model verdict on the screen
Editing a refused row adds the corrected question instead of pretending to repair the file
Remove a question, undo it, and see exactly what changed each time
The last question cannot be removed, and the refusal must be about the removal
Questions that end the same way get an advisory that never blocks and disappears when it stops being true
The counts pill after a sampled check never claims more than was measured
The free checks run out halfway: what was measured is kept and the visitor is told the rest still trains
Pre-flight against the live model: the verdict quotes the model's own answer, and an unreachable model says so
'Already known' from the preview to the settings promise to the result
Taking it home: the dataset download is the fingerprinted file, and the per-line report is read through the API/CLI
Three effort cards, no numbers: pick how hard it should try
No raw "epoch" anywhere; the trainer numbers live only in "For developers"
The side-effect check is locked on wherever publishing is possible
Where publishing is off the visitor may switch the check off — and the result says so and offers to run it
"Test with a different wording" counts the rows that have one, and off means off
Lesson name, dataset fingerprint and the per-lesson question cap on the settings screen
Press Train: one POST, 202, and the progress screen owns the lesson
Train refused (daily limit): a plain sentence, and nothing on the screen is lost
The progress screen names the stage it is in — and a demo node says "Starting…"
A real step bar and real counters — no invented percentage
Elapsed always, minutes only after three measured gradient lessons
"This lesson's log" — the trainer's own lines, with nothing private in them
Cancel training: confirm, stop, and the dataset survives
Close the tab while it trains — the lesson keeps its place and is findable again
FAILED, honestly: "there was nothing to teach"
NEEDS_MORE: the misses are listed and publishing stays shut
Fix a wrong answer and train again — new revision, new lesson, old one untouched
Continue from a dataset: "Train again" and "Add questions" from My datasets
"Train it again" from the result screen bumps the effort one step
The queue: waiting behind another lesson, and being turned away when the trainer has no room
Result screen (step 5): a demo run says it trained nothing, with the per-question "What it learned" table (Question / Before / After / Other wording)
Result screen: "What it did not learn" — the partial result names every missed question and offers the honest next step
Sampled live-model check never makes a whole-dataset claim: "Checked k of n questions in the live model — h correct"
A big result must say how much of itself it is showing: the learned/missed tables cap at 50 rows
Side effects panel: unrelated answers unchanged, the unstable-prompt caveat, and "Run the check now" when it was switched off
A lesson that changes unrelated answers is un-publishable but still keepable and downloadable
Result screen accounts for the questions that never trained: already-known and already-on-sale
Demo-node honesty: the headline says nothing was trained, and "checks were simulated" stays a different admission from "training was fake"
"Try it here": the live A/B on the private draft — with your lesson vs without it, side by side
"Try it here" fails loudly, not silently: quota, model outage and a draft that is not yours
Keep it private → Make download links: the .npz, recipe.json, RUN-LOCALLY.md, the sha256 and the 7-day expiry
"Run it on my own machine": the hardware truth first, then the node's own RUN-LOCALLY.md
Keeping a lesson private end to end: keep it on this node for 7 days, then delete it
Publish: name, price, licence, payout and the two consents → signed claim → ANNOUNCED with links to the page and the earnings
Rights declaration: publishing 100 questions or more needs the third, dataset-specific consent
Credit: the display name shown in "Shown as" must be the name the public record carries (file door)
The data-provider share: pay my key, pay my wallet, or credit me with no payment (share 0)
The published knowledge page: Taught-lesson chip, the data provider and their share, and the dataset provenance
"My datasets and lessons": dataset-first cards with fingerprint, source, retention and the four actions
Fork a dataset, and honour "delete my file as soon as training finishes"
The chat basket IS a dataset: "Your dataset · 2 questions", the file door's preview table, and a canonical .jsonl download
Freeze receipt: pressing Teach turns the basket into a file — named .jsonl, fingerprint on the dataset page, sha256 equal to the downloaded bytes
The chat body and an uploaded file produce byte-identical artifacts: POST /api/teach/jobs {facts} freezes one canonical dataset, and re-sending it makes no second copy
The frozen chat dataset appears in My datasets and can be re-trained from there (en + 한국어)
The chat basket stops at 8 corrections — a number the browser holds, not the node
The lesson carries its dataset: a signed download of exactly what it trained on, and an honest screen once the owner deletes it
CLI file door: `ainize teach dataset <file>` validates, uploads and prints every line that will not train — and a second upload makes no second copy
CLI failure contract: a refused upload still prints the per-line report, and the exit codes are 0 / 1 / 2
`ainize teach train ./file --effort quick --wait` goes from a file on disk to a finished lesson in one line, and refuses more rows than the node teaches
`teach dataset get <id> -o questions.jsonl` round-trips: the saved bytes verify against the fingerprint and re-uploading them lands on the same dataset
`teach jobs` / `teach status` from the terminal: my lessons with their dataset, the node's teaching policy, and a foreign key sees status only
OpenAPI documents every dataset route the node actually serves — path, method, auth and error codes
Quotas are counted in QUESTIONS, not lessons: rows_per_key_per_day and rows_per_ip_per_day refuse the lesson with the numbers in the message
Owner-only reads: a stranger's key, an unsigned request and a replayed signature all get 404 — and the operator can read but cannot edit someone's dataset
The rows report is the contract behind the preview table: /rows paging, status filter and summary must agree with the dataset and with the download
Operator dataset moderation: GET /api/me/teach/datasets shows who uploaded what, from which IP — and opening it is audited
Blocking a teaching key from the Teaching tab actually refuses that key's next upload and lesson
Publish review: "Review each one" holds a taught lesson at PENDING_REVIEW, and Approve / Decline reaches the teacher
Payouts to the data provider: the published anchor names the teacher with the node's share, and the operator's Payouts panel is honest about a node with no chain wallet
Teach settings on the Teaching tab: every visible knob saves, a pause reason reaches the visitor immediately, and a bad blocked-topics regex is refused
The dataset-era limits are operator-settable only through the API, and the visitor UI obeys them: file size, dataset cap, per-lesson cap and the publish declaration

product_fixes: `40c5820` teachable: fix what the dataset scenarios found (AZ-125…AZ-220) — nineteen defects, all in the "say what actually happened" family
`HEAD` teachable: the operator's lesson list pages from the newest end (AZ-218, AZ-219) — and the tests/scenarios the earlier fixes changed
not_covered: no real GPU training: every lesson came from the `stub` backend (offline placeholders, or one real fixture .npz against the live model); the `gradient` backend is exercised by no scenario here
only 12 of the 100 run against a real model (AZ-159, AZ-165, AZ-177, AZ-183, AZ-184, AZ-188, AZ-189, AZ-190, AZ-191, AZ-202, AZ-203, AZ-206); the rest are measured by the offline stub
publishing stops at node-u's local ledger — no AIN chain write, no second node fetching/verifying/buying, no real payout settlement
Korean is asserted per scenario, never swept across every screen
the mobile project is Chromium device emulation at 360x780; five scenarios carry @mobile; no Firefox/WebKit and no real device
workers=1: no two visitors teach at the same instant outside the queue scenarios
the shipped daily budgets are proven through their refusal paths, not lived through for a day
the 7-day dataset TTL, the 24-hour staged TTL and the draft TTL are asserted through expires_at and the sweep code, never by waiting
open: GET /api/me/teach/jobs is a single 500-row page (now newest-first plus every undecided lesson) with no cursor to page further back
notes: The dataset live-model legs were writing to the WRONG patch mailbox after the merge, and AZ-190 caught it. main added a `runtime.patchDir` config key and the node re-exports `ENGRAM_PATCH_DIR` to the patch hook from that value; these helpers predate the key and set only the hook's variable, so a node they started fell back to `<runtime.repo>/ple_patch` — the SHARED production mailbox — and the patch never reached the :8002 test server, which is why the live A/B measured no change. helpers/{ds-result-node,ds-train-node,ds-preview-node,ds-chat-cli-op-api}.ts now pass `NGRAM_RUNTIME_PATCH_DIR` beside `ENGRAM_PATCH_DIR`, and node-u's own config carries `runtime.patchDir=/mnt/newdata/qwen3.8/ple_patch_e2e`. AZ-190 went red -> green on that change alone.
The operator lesson-list defect (AZ-218 / AZ-219) only appears on a node that has run more than 500 lessons — the dev node had 607. A fresh node passes both scenarios with the bug present.

AZ-190 is the one scenario whose truth depends on the base model: the un-tagged 픽셀플러스 question is answered 087600 by Qwen3.8-Flash-Next on its own, so the A/B must be asked with one of the taught questions.

node-u is shared. Datasets from another session (named messy / good40 / big2500 / train12 / binary) appeared on it during this pass; every suite re-establishes its own preconditions rather than trusting the node it finds, and the runs above were unaffected.
